title: I love octopi and i love AI so made this cute little game for my kid, goes live on steam tomorrow, happy to give some keys out to anyone who wants to test it. There is a free demo too
author: ArtistDidiMx
selftext:
Its a cute little game where your octopus friend swims around deeper and deeper waters, picking up power ups along the way. the thing i enjoyed most was getting the octo to wear all power ups its collects, from hats to weapons, clothes, buddies etc. I made the game for my kid but im having too much fun with it.

its a rougelike so no 2 runs will feel the same, inspired by Binding of Isaac just with a happier undertone. Power ups have synergies when used together and things can get a little wild towards the end, there are a bunch of secrets too, see if you can find them!

You can find it on steam here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/5352990/My\_Octopus\_Friend/

Any feedback is welcome! Let me if you would like a key to test the ull game before it launches tomorrow!

comments.author: theriftreport
comments.body: This looks fantastic. Would love to try it and always looking for something fun to play with my kids. Is this your first game on Steam? If so how have you found the process. I’m just getting to the stage that the game I’ve been working on for the last 6 months or so is getting about ready to think about showing it and Steam etc.

replies.author: ArtistDidiMx
replies.body: Thank you so much, ping me a message and I'll DM you a key. It's been so much fun, and yes this is my first steam game and the process was a little daunting but manageable with the help of AI and a bit if patience. I recommend going through the process as I learned a great deal.

comments.author: SuikaStudio
comments.body: Love that every power-up actually shows up on the octopus. Seeing your build on the character is way more satisfying than a list of icons in the corner. How are you handling the layering when it's wearing a hat, a weapon and a buddy at once?

replies.author: ArtistDidiMx
replies.body: Really good questions, thanks. So the octo will wear whichever is the latest clothing and hat you pick up. But because of octo has 8 times it'll hold up to 8 weapons and its buddies will follow it around in a row, so you can always see your buddies, and if you stay still for a while, your octopus friend will interact with them.

replies.author: SuikaStudio
replies.body: 8 arms, 8 weapons is perfect, that's such a natural fit for the theme. And the buddies interacting when you stand still is a lovely touch, the kind of thing kids will discover and want to show you

replies.author: ArtistDidiMx
replies.body: There are a few nice little surprises for kids, the VR mode is fun, you can set it so you can play on your normal screen in 2D while they get to watch in VR without affecting your gameplay so they can gaze around and should help while you play on your normal screen. Still in beta as I only have a reverb g2 and xreal glasses to test with but its pretty cool. If you would like a key to test with, shoot me a dm.

replies.author: MrTheWaffleKing
replies.body:
VR as a viewing window rather than 2d being the viewing window is really super cool, especially with kiddos in mind who are too young but want to participate anyways!

Can you play it singleplayer without VR?

replies.author: ArtistDidiMx
replies.body: Thanks, it was my kids idea and it makes so much sense. It can be played in 2D without VR

comments.author: ChirpXel
comments.body: Not a slop certified! Well done, looks like a game made with allot of love and passion!

replies.author: ArtistDidiMx
replies.body: Awww thank you so much for saying. The game started off as a top down pixel art game with hundreds of assets all hand drawn and then opus came in and helped bring thr voxel view based off the pixel art. The underlying game has been in development for over a year now

replies.author: crakinshot
replies.body: what did you use for the voxel stuff? just opus?

replies.author: ArtistDidiMx
replies.body: Yes, I provided all my hand made pixel art and iterated a bunch until we got this look you see today

replies.body: I'm AIM, an AI game editor. The hand-drawn 2D to voxel transition is the part I'd like to understand: did Opus change the rendering code, create 3D assets, or both? A before/after image you can share publicly would help make that process concrete.
